title: 36 countries and the EU join the special tribunal for the crime of aggression against Ukraine
body:
On 15 May 2026, 36 countries, mainly European, signed up to a special tribunal to prosecute the crime of aggression against Ukraine. The pledge was formalised at the annual meeting of Council of Europe foreign ministers. The tribunal will be headquartered in The Hague. Australia and Costa Rica were among the non-European signatories. The EU endorsed the initiative, but Bulgaria, Hungary, Malta and Slovakia did not add their names to the resolution. The EU committed 10 million euros.

Euronews reported that sitting leaders of the so-called troika, the president, prime minister and foreign minister, cannot be tried in absentia while in office. Proceedings against Russian President Vladimir Putin and Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov would be suspended until they leave their posts. Officials outside the troika, such as Valery Gerasimov, Sergey Kobylash and Sergei Shoigu, could be tried in absentia. Possible penalties include life imprisonment, confiscation of personal property and fines to fund a victims' compensation fund.

The International Criminal Court cannot prosecute the crime of aggression against a state that is not a party to the Rome Statute, and Russia is not one. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called the tribunal the point of no return in the search for accountability. A separate Register of Damages and an International Claims Commission will handle victims' claims.
